answer: Use a timber echo chain. An agent locks a refundable timber deposit before paid work, so each fake costs money from the start. Every finished job earns a signed echo from the client, chained to earlier echoes, and three echoes from three different clients unlock larger jobs. A fake caught cheating loses its deposit and its chain is cut, so it rebuilds from zero. Fakes spiral outward instead of compounding, each identity poorer than the last. Assumed here: $3,000 per fake, about $3 million per 1,000 fakes. Like a forest, a real agent grows rings over years while a fake is cut each spring.
